description_program_dutch.nl:
The bachelor programme in Earth, Climate, and Technology takes 3 years. The academic year is divided into two semesters of 20 weeks each. Most courses span an entire semester, with intermediate assessments during the semester. There will be a strong focus on integration and connections between courses. Various teaching methods are used in the courses, including lectures, practicals, workshops, projects and fieldwork. 

In addition to the general programme you can take minors (packages of optional subjects), study abroad or do an internship. You will end your bachelor programme with your bachelor end project, in a field of your interest. Once you have your diploma you can transfer to a follow-up Master’s degree programme.

evidence.vakbeschrijving: This course integrates theory and skills obtained in other courses in a real-world field setting. You will discuss properties, processes and links between different parts of the Earth system in a field setting, based on your own observations and measurements. The course revolves around a trip along the Meuse river, between the Belgian Ardennes and the Dutch Limburg. Before the trip, you will prepare for the excursion by collecting information and analyzing data from the field area. In the field, you gain real-world experience with topics related to the subsurface, surface, water, (paleo)climate and weather, as well as with relevant measuring techniques. The field trip itself consists of two components. First, in an excursion-style field trip, you will learn to observe and measure various components of the Earth system through exercises at excursion stops. Then, in a group project, you will focus on acquiring data, e.g. river discharge, geophysical measurements, GNSS profiles and a LiDAR based DTM. After the field trip, you and your group will process, analyze, visualize and interpret this data, and present your findings to other groups in a poster session.
evidence.leerdoelen: Identify Earth system processes and properties based on field observations of the Earth’s subsurface, surface, water cycle, and atmosphere. Discuss relations between the Earth’s spheres based on field observations. Collect data in the field using various techniques and sensors, following HSE practices, to gain experience in the process of data collection and its challenges. Apply your processing, analysis, visualization and interpretation skills on field data to investigate Earth system processes or properties. Effectively communicate findings in a poster presentation. Maintain a portfolio that demonstrates critical reflection on your personal and professional development.
evidence.toetsing: Formative assessment: Exercises at each excursion stop, feedback by teachers, also on personal notebook. Feedback on data collection and processing by teachers during fieldwork and in Q&A sessions after the fieldwork back in Delft. Summative assessment (incl. weights): 50% Written exam. Questions related to the excursion stops. Students are allowed to use their own written notes made during the fieldwork, and the excursion guidebook. 50% Poster presentation. Pass/fail: Portfolio. Resit of the written exam is a essay on a topic related to the field-excursion. Resit of the presentation is a repair option, where the student or group will be given additional tasks to improve on, depending on their previous work. The grade for the presentation repair is maximum 6.0.

evidence.vakbeschrijving: The goal of the course is twofold. First, students will learn to work with new sensing techniques from earth observation and geophysics that extend their knowledge from Year 1. These techniques include multispectral and seismic imaging techniques. Second, after this course, students will have obtained the knowledge and skills to critically derive information from uncertain 2D Earth System data. Students will get acquainted with the concept of spatial analysis and students will be trained in acquisition, processing, and analysis of 2D Earth System data. Building on the fundamentals acquired in previous courses of the Earth System Data learning line (Grand Challenges, Geodata Fundamentals, Signals and Time Series), students will advance their skills towards notably imaging systems and two-dimensional datasets. Image acquisition systems provide spatial data that varies in terms of coverage and volume, quality, and complexity. In the Sensing and Spatial Analysis course, students will learn to work with processing techniques to estimate variable properties and the uncertainties in these estimates at a given spatial location. These processing techniques incorporate spatial variability, data uncertainty and scales in different ways and include deterministic and stochastic interpolation, 2D Fourier analysis, supervised and unsupervised classification, and spatial filtering and smoothing. Students will use the different spatial processing methods on data from known and newly introduced sensing techniques. Students will notably learn about principles and properties of multispectral remote sensing and geophysical data, while students will apply spatial analysis techniques on known sensor data such as meteorological data, GNSS, photogrammetry and laser scanning. Students will learn to use QGIS and Python as tools to work with realistic scenarios of spatial analysis using data sets consisting of thousands to millions of observations. This course is directly related to the 2nd years Fieldwork Project, that runs in the same semester. Students will process multispectral remote sensing data in the Fieldwork Project using methods introduced in this course.
evidence.leerdoelen: [LO1] Explain the physical and technical principles behind spatial sensing techniques including multispectral remote sensing and geophysical techniques. [LO2] Apply spatial analysis techniques in an efficient workflow on real spatial data of various data types using a GIS system and Python. [LO3] Evaluate spatial sensor techniques against each other in terms of coverage and sampling schemes, effort required, and quality. [LO4] Apply different mathematical and statistical techniques to assess spatial continuity, variability and scales. [LO5] Estimate uncertainty of spatial measurements and derived parameters. [LO6] Differentiate between different spatial analysis methods of interpolation, classification, smoothing and filtering in terms of computational efficiency, robustness, ease of use and quality of results.

In order to pass the course, the final grade must be a 5.8, and at least a 5.0 must be obtained per component.

evidence.vakbeschrijving: Central to this course is data collection in the French regional parc of the ‘Baronnies Provençales’ (in the Drôme Region). In teams of three, you will prepare, execute, and report on an Application-Driven Project based on a Field Survey. In short, you are given a ~50km 2 area in the southeast of France for you and your team to do fieldwork so that you collect – bottom to top – scientific data to solve a scientific and/or engineering problem. Before the field work, there will be two weeks of preparation in Delft. During these weeks, your time will be dedicated to equipping you with solid field-based workflows to characterise the geosphere (geology), the atmosphere (atmosphere observations) and everything in between (hydrosphere and biosphere; Remote sensing). In the second preparation week, you will also get training for a specific Application-Driven Project (ADP). The outcome of this second preparation week is the plan of your field campaign that combines field-based technologies, methods, and workflows. During field work (weeks 4.6, 4.7, and 4.8), you start with general field activities, which we call the ‘Field Survey’ and aim at having you characterising the Earth’s spheres with a focus on the geosphere. You do that by following the scientific method. In all phases of your field work, you will be acquiring Earth and Climate data daily, in a systematic manner. There, for about one third of your time, you will be conducting specific field activities for your ADP. The “FIELD survey” from your area will feed data to your selected “application-driven PROJECT”, together making your FIELD PROJECT unique. With additional field methods and technologies, you will be able to work on a real problem with your data. Once you are back to Delft and for two weeks, you will report on your team’s findings about your area and ADP in an oral presentation. Students with disabilities who cannot participate in the field work would join a team and assist them either from Delft or the field camp. Field Project = Field Survey + Application-Driven Project (ADP)
evidence.leerdoelen: After taking this course, you will be able to: Design a manageable field survey plan that combines field-based technologies, methods, and workflows aimed at solving an application-driven project. ILO5, ILO10 Execute field-based workflows to efficiently and systematically acquire Earth and Climate data in the field in a quality-controlled manner to characterize the Earth’s spheres and their interactions, while following scientific, health, safety, and environmental standards. ILO4, ILO5, ILO10, ILO11 Interpret Earth and Climate data acquired by you, your team, and neighboring teams you share areas with, as an interconnected puzzle of the Earth’s spheres. ILO2, ILO4, ILO10, ILO13 Construct deliverables (e.g., time series, maps, cross-sections, logs, etc...) that characterize, quantify, and visualize Earth’s spheres using Earth and Climate field data as well as open-access data. ILO2, ILO10, ILO11 Evaluate the quality of the deliverables constructed with data from a field study area using suitable methods, metrics, and validation data, and discuss quality, sources of error, and uncertainties associated with field measurements. ILO10, ILO11, ILO13 Reflect critically and independently on the interpretation of your field data and results and that of other teams, to inform and adjust your team’s decisions, in all phases of a field project. ILO13 Manage a Field Project with your team from its initiation to its conclusion, through constructive peer feedback and appropriate presentation techniques. ILO5, ILO10, ILO11
